newsitem.title: USA: Salomon Q1 fixed-income revs off, banking up.
newsitem.headline: Salomon Q1 fixed-income revs off, banking up.

text.p: Salomon Inc said Tuesday that fixed-income sales and trading net revenues were $519 million in the first quarter, down from $732 million a year ago, but global investment banking revenues rose over 20 percent to $220 million.
Equity sales and trading net revenues were $243 million in the quarter, up from $64 million a year ago, it said.

Net revenues from commodities trading activities, which are conducted by Phibro Inc, were $25 million in the first quarter, down from an exceptionally strong $235 million a year earlier, the company said.
Due to its cost structure, Phibro was still modestly profitable in the first quarter, Salomon said.
Beginning with this quarter, Phibro's revenues are shown as the "commodities trading" component of Salomon's revenues, it said.
Asset management revenues for the quarter were $17 million, up from $12 million a year earlier, Salomon said.
Salomon reported net income of $173 million for the first quarter, compared with income from continuing operations of $310 million a year earlier.
"Overall first quarter performance was satisfactory, with market conditions that were more difficult than generally prevailed in 1996," Chairman Robert Denham said.
In its global investment banking arm, results for debt underwriting were particularly strong, it said.
